title: Badoni's Back-to-Back Double Centuries Put Him Alongside Kohli and Gambhir
excerpt: Delhi captain Ayush Badoni followed his 217 against Gujarat with an unbeaten 210 against Jharkhand in Ranchi, becoming the 21st Indian batter to score double centuries in consecutive first-class innings.
body:
• Delhi captain Ayush Badoni scored an unbeaten 210 off 228 balls against Jharkhand at the JSCA International Stadium in Ranchi.
  • It followed his 217 against Gujarat in Delhi's previous match, making him the 21st Indian batter with double centuries in consecutive first-class innings.
  • Badoni and Sumit Mathur (150 not out) added an unbroken 334 runs for the sixth wicket as Delhi declared at 515 for 5.
  • Jharkhand reached 131 for 4 at stumps on day two, trailing by 384 runs, with Utkarsh Singh unbeaten on 53.

Ayush Badoni has done something only two other Delhi batters have managed before him. The 26-year-old captain struck an unbeaten 210 against Jharkhand in the Ranji Trophy on Tuesday, his second double century in consecutive first-class innings, joining Virat Kohli and Gautam Gambhir in the elite list for Delhi.

Badoni's innings, off 228 balls with 19 fours and three sixes, was the defining performance of day two at the JSCA International Stadium in Ranchi, according to Wisden's round-three report. Delhi resumed in a competitive position and Badoni turned it into a commanding one.

A 334-run stand that broke the game open

Delhi's top order had given the innings a start — Priyansh Arya made 39, Sanat Sangwan 37 and Yash Dhull 29 — before Badoni took the attack to Jharkhand's bowlers. He reached 200 in only 216 balls and, with Sumit Mathur, added an unbeaten 334 runs for the sixth wicket. Mathur finished on 150 not out as Delhi declared at 515 for 5 in 130 overs.

The declaration was justified quickly. Delhi's attack reduced Jharkhand to 131 for 4 in 47 overs by stumps, with Utkarsh Singh's unbeaten 53 the hosts' main resistance. Jharkhand trail by 384 runs going into day three.

Form that has been building

This was no isolated innings. In Delhi's previous match against Gujarat, Badoni made 217 as Delhi posted 648 for 8 declared — a game in which Priyansh Arya scored 199 and Mathur 92, before Gujarat replied with 479. Badoni has now recorded four double centuries in his first-class career, including one for North Zone in this season's Duleep Trophy, according to Circle of Cricket.

A day of big scores across the Ranji Trophy

Badoni's was not the only landmark innings in round three. Baroda's Priyanshu Moliya made 321, Chandigarh's Nehal Pajni scored a double century as his side posted 685, and Madhya Pradesh's Saransh Jain took 13 wickets in the match against Bihar, according to Wisden's round wrap. Bengal's Shahbaz Ahmed made 121 and took two wickets against Kerala, where Mohammed Shami claimed three. The volume of runs underlined the strength of Badoni's achievement rather than diminishing it: double centuries came in clusters on day two, but only his completed a back-to-back pair in consecutive innings — and only his came with the captaincy attached, in a match his side now controls.

What it means

Consecutive double centuries are rare enough — Badoni is only the 21st Indian to achieve the feat — that selectors notice. Leading the side while scoring at this volume strengthens his case in a crowded field of young Indian middle-order batters. Delhi, meanwhile, are in control of this match: a first-innings lead is within reach on day three if their bowlers finish the job.
